chapter: Miles, Donald Byrd, Newport Youth Band and first gigs
title: Newport Youth Band members and what it taught
summary: He lists band alumni, including Larry Rosen and Eddie Gomez, the dances played in New England and the band ending around 1960.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Okay. So, I’m sorry, but could you talk about the Newport Youth Band?

So, in the Newport Youth Band there are a number of musicians who became professional musicians. There were three trumpet players, you know, this is besides myself, and trombonists. They worked with people like Slide Hampton, Maynard Ferguson, Woody Herman, you know? The pianist is someone who writes lots of music, Michael Benny. The drummer was Larry Rosen, who started GRP records. Him and his partner Dave Grusin built that record company up and then sold it for 40 million dollars.

It was just the two of them! So, the education that we got at the Newport Youth Band was very, very important. The bass player, Eddie Gomez, is around. Of the people who are around now, it’s just Eddie Gomez, baritone saxophonist Ronnie Cuber, and myself, and Michael Benny. That’s it.

We performed all over. We did dances all up and down the east coast, mostly in the New England area. Sometimes, we’d have to stay off from school on a Monday or on a Friday, which was always nice. We’d ride the bus, our bus, we’d ride the bus, you know? So, it was really giving us and understanding of what a professional musician’s life was all about.
While you were still in high school?

Yeah, still in high school. I left the band—well, actually the band broke up by about 1960. So, my last year in high school was meant just to make up all of the bad grades that I had received so I could graduate with some kind of good grades.
